title: Screen locker takes a second of black screen to activate
line: Locking goes from black straight to the lock screen's wallpaper instead of fading the clock in on a black screen first, though the short black before it remains.
explanation: KWin blanks the screen as soon as the session locks and keeps it black until kscreenlocker_greet has started and drawn its first frame. The greeter made the end of that black worse: it loaded the lock screen QML before setting the view's resize mode, so the view shrank to the QML's 800x600 implicit size and the wallpaper was decoded at 800x600 and then again at the screen size; meanwhile the lock screen's 800 ms fade-in started at creation, so the clock faded in on black before the wallpaper arrived. The greeter now sets the resize mode before loading the QML, so the wallpaper is decoded once at the right size as the window is first shown, and the lock screen starts its fade-in only once the wallpaper reports it has loaded (or after one second, if a wallpaper plugin never does), so the first non-black frame is the wallpaper with the clock fading in over it.

commits.message:
greeter: set the resize mode before loading the lock screen

The default mode resized the view to the lock screen's 800x600 implicit
size, so the wallpaper was first decoded at that size and again once the
screen size came back, delaying it after locking. Set it before loading.

CCBUG: 520995

lockscreen: fade in once the wallpaper has loaded

The lock screen started its fade-in as soon as it was created, so the
clock faded in on a black screen while the wallpaper was still loading.
Start the fade once the wallpaper has loaded, or after a second at most.

CCBUG: 520995

media.caption: Master, frames from the last desktop frame (30 fps screencast): black, then the clock on black, then the wallpaper with the clock already half faded in.
With the fix, black goes straight to the wallpaper, with the clock fading in over it.
Locking with the fix, half speed.
Previous version of the patch with a test wallpaper plugin that never finishes loading: the lock screen stays blank, even after pressing Shift.
With the one-second fallback, same plugin: the clock fades in and Shift shows the password field.

review.text: This patchset does not fix Bug 520995 (the ~0.5-1 s black screen when locking): both commits only use CCBUG: 520995 and the measurements and frame strips confirm the black-screen duration is unchanged (~0.57-0.87 s vs 0.47-0.93 s on master, with the wallpaper arriving at the exact same +567 ms and pure black lasting 33 ms longer). It only masks a brief clock-on-black transition rather than addressing greeter startup latency or the lock transition itself. Additionally, holding lockScreenRoot.opacity at 0 in LockScreenUi.qml until wallpaperLoaded or the 1 s fallback fires can hide the password prompt if the user wakes the lock screen (uiVisible) while a slow wallpaper is still loading.
changes: Actually address the reported black-screen startup delay (e.g., reducing kscreenlocker_greet startup latency or redesigning the KWin/kscreenlocker lock transition with maintainer buy-in) so a commit legitimately closes the bug with BUG: 520995 rather than leaving it unfixed with CCBUG.
If the 1-line kscreenlocker setResizeMode reorder is still desired on its own to avoid redundant 800x600 wallpaper decoding, submit it as an independent cleanup rather than as a fix for 520995.

If delaying the LockScreenUi fade-in is kept in a separate polish MR, ensure waking the UI (uiVisible becoming true) immediately reveals lockScreenRoot instead of keeping the password prompt invisible for up to 1 s while the wallpaper loads.

reviews.text: Both commits are clean, well-placed polish (setting SizeRootObjectToView before setSource avoids the 800x600 double decode; the fade now waits for wallpaper.loading with a 1 s fallback), and after-1.png shows the clock-on-black stage gone. But the bug is the ~0.5-1 s of plain black before the lock screen appears, and the evidence shows that black unchanged (0.53-0.87 s after vs 0.47-0.93 s before); both commits only use CCBUG, so the reported problem is not closed. Minor: keeping lockScreenRoot at opacity 0 for up to a second hides the UI while it still takes keystrokes, which is acceptable but worth noting in the MR.
changes: Actually remove or substantially shorten the black between locking and the greeter's first frame (e.g. KWin keeps showing the last desktop frame or a blurred snapshot under the lock until the greeter has presented, or a pre-started/faster greeter), then use BUG: 520995
Re-measure the black interval before/after to prove it is gone; if the remaining two commits are submitted on their own, keep them as CCBUG polish separate from the bug-closing fix
